lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rainfall FM. Ninety point one. It's raining. It's lovely.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: You're listening to Rainfall FM, from the Damp Dimension. Bring a towel. Bring two.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rainfall FM, through the night and through the rain, which round here is the same thing.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: This is Rainfall FM. Four thousand years of drizzle, and we've never once run out.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Good morning from Rainfall FM. It's raining. I only mention it so you're not surprised.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rainfall FM. The kettle's on. The kettle is always on.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rainfall FM. If you can hear the rain louder than usual, your window's open. Close it, love. Or don't. It's nice.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Here are tonight's rainfall totals. Precinct One, two inches. Precinct Four, two inches. That's a draw. Precinct Nine, three and a half inches, a convincing win at home.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: And Precinct Twelve, nought.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Nought? I'm being told Precinct Twelve has fallen into the canal. Recount pending.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: A listener asks what the sun is like. I've never seen it, love. From what I've read, it's a sort of very large lamp that nobody's in charge of.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Sounds stressful. I'll stick with the drizzle. Here's a song.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Kettle's just boiled, so I'll keep this short. That last one was by a band who recorded entirely under a bus shelter. You could hear the number nine going past at the end. Lovely. Here's another.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: A reminder about umbrella etiquette. If two floating umbrellas meet on a narrow street, the smaller umbrella goes underneath.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: If they're the same size, they stay where they are, hovering, until one of them apologises. There are two on Lantern Street that have been there since spring.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: It's half past something, the rain's doing that thing where it sounds like applause, and I've decided to take it personally.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Thank you. Thank you very much. You're too kind. Here's the next one.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Morning, all. Visibility is low, spirits are fair, and the gutters on Lantern Street are singing in the key of D. Here's something to drink your tea to.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: We've had a letter from someone who lives in a place where it doesn't rain. They say the air is just... empty. Nothing in it at all.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: I've read it three times. I think it's the most frightening thing anyone has ever sent me. Let's have some music.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rainfall FM is sponsored by Grumbel's Ladders. Non-slip rungs, tested in every weather we have, which is one weather. Grumbel's. Up is a choice. Mind the puddle at the bottom.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Shadow owners, take note. In this light nobody's got a shadow, so if yours has gone missing, you won't notice for weeks.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: But if he answers to Greg, a man in Precinct Six says one's been sheltering under his awning. Polite. Bit damp. Wouldn't say where he was headed. Hollis, the porch light's on, I take it.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Evening, everyone. There's lightning very far off to the north. Not our lightning. Someone else's. We wave at it anyway. It's only neighbourly. Here's a song.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: That last song was about a dry sock. You can always tell. There's a sort of longing in the bass. Coming up, a song about a wet sock, which is all the others.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: If you're listening in bed, the sound on your roof right now is the same sound that's on mine. That's about the closest thing we've got to holding hands across the city. Here's a slow one.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Puddle report. The big one outside the bakery has now been given a name, a postcode and a small boat.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Please don't fish in it. We don't know what's in there, and frankly, neither does the puddle.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Afternoon. Same as the morning, but wetter round the edges. If you've the day off, put a towel on the radiator and just be a person for a bit. Here's some music for that.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Four thousand years of rain, and do you know, I've never once been bored of it. Every drop's a slightly different shape. I've been counting. I'm on eleven. Here's the next song.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: For the night shift: the tram drivers, the bakers, the woman who wipes the condensation off the bus stop map so we can all see where we are. This one's for you. Thank you for the map.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: And now the forecast. Tonight, rain, heavy at times, lighter at others, and at about three in the morning, a sort of thoughtful drizzle.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Tomorrow, rain. The weekend, we'll see. It'll be rain.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Nineteen years I've been reading this, and I still read it like it might say something else. Rainfall FM. Stay dry. Or stay damp and happy. Both count.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: This is the Night Tram, on Rainfall FM. The last tram home through Precinct Nine. Mind the gap. It's full of water.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: The number nine is coming down Lantern Street, lit up like a fish tank. Four passengers. One asleep, one reading, one doing the crossword.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: And one just looking out at the rain, the way you do on the last tram. This one's for her.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: The driver on the night route is called Ferdinand. He's driven it for thirty years, and every night, at the bottom of Gutter Hill, he rings the bell twice for no reason.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: He says it's for the puddles. Here's one for Ferdinand.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Good morning. It's the Kettle Hour, on Rainfall FM. The kettle's on, and it's raining. Both of those are always true.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: The morning totals. Precinct One, an inch and a half. Precinct Four, an inch and a half. Another draw.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: They're getting very good at draws, Precinct One and Four. I think they're friends now.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: If you've just woken up, the rain on your window is the same rain that was there when you went to sleep. It waited up for you.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Isn't that nice. Here's something to drink your tea to.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rainfall FM. Still raining. Still lovely. Still here.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: That was lovely, wasn't it. Like rain on a shed roof.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Evening, all. Or morning. It's hard to tell under this much cloud.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Kettle's just boiled, so I'll keep this short.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Puddle news. The big one outside the bakery has been given a lighthouse. Very small. Very bright. Several ducks have said thank you.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: The Drainpipe Choir were in the studio this afternoon. They don't sing, as such. They stand under the gutter and let it happen. It's beautiful. It's very damp.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Umbrella news. The two umbrellas on Lantern Street, hovering since spring, have finally sorted it out. They've decided to share. They're one big umbrella now, and they seem very happy.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: A listener writes that she saw the sun once, through a gap in the clouds, for about a second. She says it was very bright, and she isn't sure she approves.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Mizzle have a new record out. It's mostly the sound of a tin roof. If you've ever lain awake under a tin roof, you'll know why it went straight to number one.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: A reminder from the Precinct Nine Tidy Streets Committee. Please don't empty your wellies on the tram. Empty them into the gutter on the way home. The gutter is very grateful.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Here's the next one. Stay damp, everyone.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Here's some music. Put the kettle on, love.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rainfall FM. Here's another one, straight from the gutter.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Listen to that. Lovely. Here's some more.

clips.title: Greg Comes Home, Part Four: Nobody Here Has a Shadow

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: We've a visitor at the studio tonight. He came down through the only gap in the clouds we've had all year, on a moonbeam, and landed in the big puddle outside the bakery. It's Greg.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Hello. Sorry about the puddle.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: The puddle's fine, love. It's had worse. How are you finding Precinct Nine?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Dark. Every time I go outside, I sort of disappear.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: That's the clouds. Nobody here has a shadow. You're the first one most of Precinct Nine has ever met.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: People keep stopping to look at me.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: They think you're beautiful. Like a sunset that walks about.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: I need to get to the eastern Overlap. I'm going home. But I can't go anywhere without a light.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Then take the night tram. Ferdinand drives it. The number nine has big front lamps, and they'll throw you all the way to the edge of the precinct.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Will he mind?

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Ferdinand? He rings the bell for puddles, love. He'll be thrilled.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: That's him now. Go on. Sit up at the front, in the light.

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Thank you, Drizzle.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: And Greg? Your fella's porch light. Is it on?

lines.speaker: Greg, a Shadow
lines.text: Every night, they say.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Then you'll be fine. Here's one for the road. It's wet.

clips.title: Teodor Is Heard, Part Ten: Rain at Relay Four

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: It's nearly three in the morning, and Precinct Nine is doing something it's never done. Every window on Lantern Street is open. Every light is on.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Teodor at Relay Four has a little crystal radio now. It can just about hear, if something carries the signal all the way out to him.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: And round here, love, we've got plenty of something that goes everywhere.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Rain. So at three o'clock, we're all going to lean out of our windows, say it into the rain, and let the rain take it. Here we go. Ferdinand's ringing the bell.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Yes.

lines.speaker: Lantern Street
lines.text: Yes!

lines.speaker: Lantern Street
lines.text: Yes, Teodor.

lines.speaker: Lantern Street
lines.text: Yes, love.

lines.speaker: Ferdinand, Tram Driver
lines.text: Yes!

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: Relay Four. Night four thousand and forty. Something odd. It's raining here.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: It never rains at Relay Four. And the rain is saying something. On the roof. On the window. On Captain, who is not pleased.

lines.speaker: Teodor, Relay Four
lines.text: It sounds like. It sounds a lot like yes.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: It is, love. It's from all of us. Close your windows, everybody. And Teodor? Put a towel down. It's our rain. It gets everywhere.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Halloween in Precinct Nine. The children go trick or treating in wellies. The ghosts go out in sheets, and come home in very wet sheets.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Nobody's frightened. Everybody's damp. Here's a spooky one. It's also wet.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: The Halloween forecast. Rain, heavy at times, with a ghostly mist at about midnight.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: That's just the rain, standing still for a moment, thinking about its life. Leave it be. It'll start falling again when it's ready.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Moon Goes Missing

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Somebody's lost a moon, apparently. Everyone's ringing in about it.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: We've not seen a moon in Precinct Nine for four thousand years, love, so it's not ours. Hope it turns up. Kettle's on, just in case.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: It smells of toast. Everywhere, they're saying. Even here, and you can't make toast in Precinct Nine. It goes soggy on the way to the plate.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Somebody's managed it somewhere. Good for them.

clips.title: The Convergence: The Song Nobody Can Finish

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: There's a song going round everybody's head, and nobody knows the end.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: I think the rain knows it. It keeps tapping out the first bit on the window, and stopping, like it's being polite.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Three knocks at the studio door just then. Nobody there. Just the rain, stood on the step.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Come in, love. Wipe your feet. Not that it helps.

clips.title: The Convergence: A Colour With No Name

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: The clouds parted for a second, and the sky behind them was a colour I've never seen. Neither has anyone.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: Then they closed again, quite quickly, like they'd shown us something they shouldn't have.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: There's a pigeon in the studio. Wet through, bless it. Walked in like it had a key.

lines.speaker: Drizzle Montgomery
lines.text: It's sat by the kettle, looking at me as if we've met. Maybe we have.
